name: Tool-to-Agent Retrieval: Bridging Tools and Agents for Scalable LLM Multi-Agent Systems
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2511.01854, cs.CL); not peer-reviewed. Submitted 3 Nov 2025, last revised 4 Nov 2025 (v2). DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2511.01854.
authors_affiliation: Elias Lumer, Faheem Nizar, Anmol Gulati, Pradeep Honaganahalli Basavaraju, and Vamse Kumar Subbiah. Affiliation: PricewaterhouseCoopers U.S.A. (PwC). The same author cluster (Lumer, Gulati, Subbiah, Basavaraju, Burke) authored ScaleMCP, Toolshed, Graph RAG-Tool Fusion, and MemTool, all from PwC.
code_url: N/A (no official code repository for Tool-to-Agent Retrieval located; only the sibling ScaleMCP repo exists at github.com/EliasLumer/ScaleMCP, which is a different paper). The evaluation reuses the public LiveMCPBench data (github.com/icip-cas/LiveMCPBench, annotated_data/all_annotations.json) credited in the references.) [uncertain]
maintained_repo_url: N/A (no maintained leaderboard/paper-list released for this method; the benchmark it uses, LiveMCPBench, is maintained at https://icip-cas.github.io/LiveMCPBench by a separate group.)
task_domain: tool-use (LLM tool / MCP-server retrieval and routing) for multi-agent systems; large-scale tool / agent selection.
problem_setting: Inference-time, interactive multi-agent setting. A top-level assistant orchestrates specialized sub-agents, each of which is an MCP server bundling dozens to thousands of tools. Given a user query (or its decomposed sub-steps), the system must route to the right entity: a specific tool when the query is fine-grained, or an entire agent/MCP bundle when broader capability helps. The authors argue existing pipelines force a brittle two-stage choice: agent-first routing (match coarse agent descriptions, then operate within that agent, hiding relevant tools) vs tool-only retrieval (ignores complementary tools in the same bundle). No LLM fine-tuning; off-the-shelf embedding models are used. Supervision for evaluation is the ground-truth tool-agent mapping per (sub-)step in LiveMCPBench; the retriever itself is not trained. The tool/agent store is static (the 70-server / 527-tool LiveMCPBench catalog).
what_is_retrieved: tools and agents: individual tool names/descriptions AND their parent agents (MCP servers), both embedded in one shared space and linked by metadata (tool -> owner agent).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a unified tool-agent catalog built offline over MCP server names/descriptions and their tool names/descriptions (LiveMCPBench: 70 MCP servers, 527 tools). It is not a growing/episodic memory the agent writes to during task execution.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Top-K ranking objective (top-K unique agents), but reformulated for completeness/coverage of the needed agents on multi-step tasks: tool-level retrieval feeds a top-N candidate list which is then traversed to parent agents and de-duplicated to top-K unique agents. The goal is to surface the correct agent(s)/MCP server(s) for each sub-step (each question averages 1.40 MCP agents and 2.82 tools across 2.68 steps), evaluated with Recall/mAP/nDCG @{1,3,5} rather than a fixed single-tool top-1.
retrieval_unit: tool-API and agent: a single tool (name + description, an API call/function/action) OR an entire agent/MCP server (name + description bundling a coherent toolset). Tools are linked to their owning agent via metadata edges in a bipartite tool-agent graph G=(A,T,E).
index_source: Static, offline-constructed unified store. The tool-agent catalog C is composed of a tool corpus C_T (tool names/descriptions, each carrying owner(T)=A metadata) and an agent corpus C_A (agent names/descriptions as parent nodes). Built once over the LiveMCPBench catalog; not induced online/test-time.
index_structure_topology: Bipartite graph / hierarchical (agent -> owned tools) layered on top of a joint flat vector index. Tools and agents share one vector space; explicit ownership edges (tool -> parent agent) enable traversal from a retrieved tool up to its executable agent. Modeled as a bipartite graph G=(A,T,E) with E = ownership relations.
retriever_type: Hybrid: dense vector retrieval combined with lexical BM25 over the unified tool-agent catalog (semantic + lexical matching for recall). Evaluated across 8 embedding models (Vertex AI text-embedding-005, Gemini Embedding 001, Amazon Titan embed text v1/v2, OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 / 3-small / 3-large, all-MiniLM-L6-v2).
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf): the retriever uses pretrained embedding models plus BM25 with no contrastive training, LM-feedback, preference learning, or RL of the retriever. The novelty is the indexing/traversal design (joint tool-agent space + metadata links), not a trained retriever.
query_construction: Two evaluated paradigms: (1) Direct Querying - the user's high-level question is used directly as the retrieval query without preprocessing; (2) Step-wise Querying - the query is decomposed into a sequence of sub-tasks, each submitted independently to the retriever (the primary setting in the evaluation). The retriever input may be the original query, the decomposed sub-steps, or a combination. Query rewriting is cited as a complementary lever.
query_granularity: Both task-level (Direct Querying, one query for the whole task) and step/sub-task-level (Step-wise Querying, one query per decomposed sub-step). Step-wise is the primary setting; it constructs a query per sub-step so different agents can be retrieved across a multi-step workflow.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative (step-wise) in the primary setting: retrieval is performed once per decomposed sub-step. In the Direct Querying variant it is one-shot at the task level. Retrieval is decoupled from generation and run before equipping the chosen tool/agent.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval fires deterministically per query / per decomposed sub-step (one retrieval call per step in step-wise mode). It is not gated by token-level confidence, attention/uncertainty, a learned complexity classifier, reflection tokens, or an explicit agent-initiated request.
reranking: Two-stage selection acting as a rerank/aggregation: retrieve top-N (N >> K) entities from the joint catalog by hybrid similarity, then map each tool hit to its parent agent (metadata traversal), aggregate, and select the top-K unique agents (Algorithm 1). This tool->agent owner-aggregation is the reranking-equivalent step; no learned cross-encoder or RRF reranker is described.
retrieved_context_refinement: Selection/de-duplication via tool-to-agent traversal: from the top-N ranked entities, owner-map each retrieved tool to its agent, skip entries with missing/undefined owners, and keep only top-K unique agents. No reason-in-documents distillation, compression, or distractor-filtering classifier beyond this de-duplication.
how_retrieved_used: Routing / prompt augmentation: the retrieved top-K agents (and, where the query is fine-grained, the specific tool) are returned to equip the LLM agent for execution - deciding what to equip (a single tool vs an entire agent bundle) in one pass. The paper evaluates the retrieval stage (Recall/mAP/nDCG) rather than downstream task execution.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-route within a hierarchical multi-agent pipeline: a unified one-pass retrieval narrows to top-K agents/tools, then the system routes (equips a tool or an agent). Under step-wise querying, retrieval interleaves with the query decomposition (one retrieval per sub-step), aligning with reasoning-based retrieval-planning. It is not embedded inside MCTS/tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per sub-task / per decomposed step (step-wise querying): retrieval is woven in at the granularity of each decomposed sub-goal of the query. In the Direct Querying variant it is per-answer (one retrieval for the whole task). Not per-CoT-token.
retrieved_item_representation: Structured tool / agent metadata: the surface form is tool names + descriptions (and their owner-agent links) and agent names + descriptions. Not a distilled strategy, free-text workflow, executable program, or latent token; the retrieved entity is a tool or an executable agent reference.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Two coexisting abstraction levels in one space: fine-grained tool/API capability descriptions AND coarser agent/MCP-server bundle descriptions. The method deliberately spans both - procedural tool specification at the low level and an agent-bundle capability summary at the high level - bridged by ownership links.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Context-dilution mitigation by design: jointly indexing tools and agents (rather than chunking many tools into one coarse agent description) preserves fine-grained tool semantics while retaining agent context; metadata traversal recovers the executable agent without collapsing tools into a single diluted summary. No retriever-aware training, relevance evaluator, or distractor-aware SFT is used; robustness is structural (joint linked index) rather than learned.
memory_type: none (static external tool-agent catalog/index; no episodic, skill-library, workflow, procedural, or latent memory written by the agent). The store is a fixed, structured knowledge base of tools and agents.
write_back: False - the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills from execution. The catalog is built offline from the MCP server/tool descriptions; no agent write-back of trajectories or outcomes is described.
online_growth: No: the retrievable store is frozen after offline catalog construction. (The cited sibling work ScaleMCP adds CRUD auto-synchronization with MCP servers, but Tool-to-Agent Retrieval as evaluated uses the static LiveMCPBench catalog and does not grow from deployment experience.)
write_back_trigger: Never: no experience/case write-back occurs. Any catalog change would be external re-indexing of tool/agent metadata, not triggered by task success or failure during deployment.
failure_experience_usage: None: failed or negative experiences are not stored or retrieved; the method maintains no success-vs-failure case memory and learns no corrective rules. It is a static retrieval method, not an experience-accumulating one.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only at the index level at most (catalog can be rebuilt/extended with new tool/agent metadata); stored entries are not mutated, merged, refined, or pruned by the system from experience. No experience-driven evolution.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: retrieval is a fixed hybrid (BM25 + dense) similarity ranking followed by deterministic top-N -> parent-agent traversal -> top-K unique-agent selection (Algorithm 1). It is not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval/selection policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Partial / by design at the catalog level: the unified tool-agent index spans many MCP servers (agents) and is shared across the multi-agent system for routing, so all agents draw from one common linked store. However, there is no sharing of learned experience/memory across agents - the shared object is a static retrieval catalog, not accumulated episodic memory.
benchmarks: LiveMCPBench (Mo et al., 2025, arXiv:2508.01780): 70 MCP servers, 527 tools, and 95 real-world questions annotated with step-by-step breakdowns and relevant tool-agent mappings (avg 2.68 steps, 2.82 tools, 1.40 MCP agents per question). An additional agent-only baseline dataset (MCP server names + descriptions only) is constructed to isolate the contribution of tool-level information.
benchmark_family: tool (MCP tool/agent retrieval; LiveMCPBench - 'an ocean of MCP tools'). Repurposes a multi-server tool-use benchmark for intrinsic retrieval evaluation.
baselines: BM25; Q.Retrieval (query/agent-only dense retrieval baseline); MCPZero (MCP-Zero, Fei et al. 2025, arXiv:2506.01056, active tool discovery / agent-first routing); ScaleMCP (Lumer et al. 2025, arXiv:2505.06416, dynamic auto-synchronizing MCP tool retriever). MCPZero and ScaleMCP are the previous state-of-the-art agent retrievers compared against.
key_metrics: Recall@K, mean Average Precision (mAP@K), and normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (nDCG@K) for K in {1,3,5}. Retrieval accuracy = retrieved agents vs ground-truth agents per (sub-)query. No downstream task-success metric is reported (retrieval-stage evaluation only).
headline_result: On LiveMCPBench, Tool-to-Agent Retrieval reaches Recall@5 = 0.83 and nDCG@5 = 0.46 (Recall@1 0.61, @3 0.77; nDCG@1 0.61, @3 0.56; mAP@5 0.34), beating the best baseline ScaleMCP (Recall@5 0.74, nDCG@5 0.40) and MCPZero (Recall@5 0.70, nDCG@5 0.41). The paper headlines aggregate gains over previous SOTA of 19.4% in Recall@5 and 17.7% in nDCG@5 (NOTE: the abstract states '19.4% Recall@5 and 17.7% nDCG@5' while the Contributions section reports the same two numbers swapped - '17.7% recall@5 and 19.4% nDCG@5'; the percentages are internally inconsistent in the paper) [uncertain].
ablations: Embedding-model sweep (Table 2): per-embedding comparison vs MCPZero across 8 models, all showing gains - strongest on Amazon Titan v2 (Recall@5 0.66 -> 0.85, +28% relative) and even compact all-MiniLM-L6-v2 +13%; very stable improvements (std 0.02 Recall@5, 0.01 nDCG@5 vs MCPZero), indicating architecture-agnostic gains driven by the unified indexing rather than a specific embedding. Agent-only-vs-joint analysis: an agent-only baseline dataset isolates tool-level contribution; the authors report 39.13% of retrieved top-K items came from the agent corpus C_A and 34.44% of matched top-K tools also traced back to C_A, evidencing the lift is from the joint tool+agent index, not tool retrieval alone. Query-paradigm comparison: Direct vs Step-wise Querying (step-wise is primary). No separate component-removal of BM25 vs dense is tabulated.
evaluation_decoupling: Fully decoupled to the intrinsic retrieval side: only intrinsic IR metrics (Recall@K, mAP@K, nDCG@K) are reported; the work evaluates the retrieval/routing stage in isolation and does NOT report end-to-end downstream task success (e.g., LiveMCPBench's LLM-as-Judge task-success). So there is no end-to-end metric to decouple from - it is retrieval-metric-only.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Process-level retrieval quality only: step-wise (sub-step-level) retrieval accuracy via Recall/mAP/nDCG. No final task-outcome metric and no reasoning-faithfulness scoring; evaluation targets step-level retrieval correctness against annotated tool-agent mappings.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Motivated by token/prompt-cost reduction at scale (one MCP server with 26 tools can exceed 4,600 tokens, so forwarding all tool descriptions is impractical), and the method enables one-pass retrieval to avoid a brittle two-stage agent-first-then-tool pipeline. However, no concrete latency, token-cost, or retrieval-call-count numbers are reported for Tool-to-Agent Retrieval itself; the efficiency argument is qualitative (avoid context dilution, single-pass decision). [uncertain]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Two cutoffs: retrieve top-N (N >> K) candidate entities from the joint catalog, then de-duplicate by parent agent to a fixed top-K unique agents (K reported at 1, 3, 5). Selection is reranked-then-truncated to K unique agents; no explicit injected-token budget cap is stated (the downstream prompt budget motivates the approach but is not quantified for the method). N is described as N >> K but a specific N value is not given. [uncertain]
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (method/system paper, not a survey or taxonomy).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Not a benchmark-contribution paper. It reuses LiveMCPBench (70 MCP servers, 527 tools, 95 human-annotated real-world questions with step-by-step tool-agent mappings; avg 2.68 steps / 2.82 tools / 1.40 agents per question) and additionally derives an agent-only variant (MCP server names + descriptions only) to isolate tool-level information. Best system here (Tool-to-Agent) reaches Recall@5 0.83 / nDCG@5 0.46, leaving substantial headroom, signaling the retrieval task remains hard.
builds_on: ScaleMCP (Lumer et al. 2025, arXiv:2505.06416) and Toolshed / RAG-Tool Fusion (Lumer et al. 2024, arXiv:2410.14594) and Graph RAG-Tool Fusion (Lumer et al. 2025, arXiv:2502.07223) by the same PwC team; MCP-Zero (Fei et al. 2025) for agent-first active tool discovery; classic RAG (Gao et al. 2024 survey) and BM25 (Robertson & Zaragoza 2009) + hybrid semantic-lexical retrieval (Kuzi et al. 2020); graph/KG-augmented retrieval (Think-on-Graph, Graph CoT, HybridRAG, KG+LLM roadmap, Graph-RAG survey). Evaluated on LiveMCPBench (Mo et al. 2025).
contrasts_with: Agent-first / hierarchical pipelines that match a brief agent description then operate only within that agent (e.g., MCP-Zero, hierarchical MCP-server-then-tool routing) - which can hide relevant fine-grained tools; tool-only retrieval that treats each tool independently and ignores the surrounding agent bundle (e.g., Toolshed/ToolRet-style top-k tool retrieval); ScaleMCP and Q.Retrieval as agent-level retrievers; graph-only tool organizers (ToolNet, ControlLLM); iterative tool retrieval (ToolReAGT, ProTIP). The contrast is explicitly the brittle two-stage tool-only-vs-agent-first choice versus a single joint linked space.
lineage: Group E (tool-use), MCP-era tool/agent retrieval lineage from the PwC team (Toolshed/RAG-Tool Fusion -> Graph RAG-Tool Fusion -> ScaleMCP / MemTool -> Tool-to-Agent Retrieval). It advances scalable tool retrieval from tool-only or agent-only routing toward a unified, metadata-linked tool+agent vector space for multi-agent orchestration, descending from Gorilla/ToolLLM-style API-doc retrieval and classic RAG, and intersecting graph-based tool organization.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle - it retrieves static tool/agent metadata, not problem-solution cases).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it is framed as retrieval/routing for tool-and-agent selection.
tool_document_engineering: Modest: tool entries are indexed from tool names + descriptions with explicit owner(T)=A parent-agent metadata; agent entries from agent names + descriptions. No synthetic-query augmentation or weighted-field embeddings are applied in this method (the related ScaleMCP's Tool Document Weighted Average / TDWA and synthetic-question augmentation are cited but not the core lever here). The key engineering is the dual tool-corpus + agent-corpus indexing and tool->agent ownership links.
index_content_separation: Partial / by design: a lightweight retrievable index entry (tool/agent name + description + owner metadata) is separated from the heavier executable agent context (authentication, parameter inference, access policies) maintained at the agent level and resolved via traversal when an entity is selected. This is a progressive-disclosure-flavored separation but not explicitly framed as an SOP-index-then-content scheme.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Protocol: Model Context Protocol (MCP) - agents are MCP servers and tools are their exposed functions/API calls. The index as evaluated is a STATIC offline catalog over LiveMCPBench (no live CRUD auto-synchronization in this paper; auto-sync is the contribution of the cited sibling ScaleMCP, not of Tool-to-Agent Retrieval).
tool_dependency_awareness: Partial: the method models tool->agent OWNERSHIP relations as a bipartite graph (G=(A,T,E)) and traverses them, and motivates retaining agent context (authentication, parameter inference, access policies) and cross-connected operations within a server. But it does not model inter-tool data-flow dependencies (output-of-A feeds B) or build a tool-prerequisite dependency graph; the modeled relation is tool-to-parent-agent ownership, not tool-to-tool dependency.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no CBR case adaptation; retrieved tool/agent metadata is used as-is for routing/equipping).
